newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stockholm bourse's '96 pre-tax profit rises 21 pct.
newsitem.headline: Stockholm bourse's '96 pre-tax profit rises 21 pct.

text.p: The Stockholm Stock Exchange reported on Tuesday that its pre-tax profit rose 21 percent to 110 million crowns in 1996 from 91 million crowns in 1995.
The bourse said share trading on the exchange rose by 38 percent to 918 billion crowns.
The net export of Swedish shares continued to rise and overseas players accounted for a third of the turnover.
"The rate of turnover (monthly average) increased to 66 percent from 61 percent, which is a high level internationally," the bourse said in a statement.
The board of the stock exchange said it proposed to lift its annual dividend to 20 crowns from 10.
Income rose to 222 million crowns last year from 182 million in 1995, while operating profit rose to 95 million from 77 million.
During 1996, nine new members were added to the bourse, of which six were remote members, while five members left.
At the end of 1996, the bourse had a total of 45 members, up from 41 a year earlier.

The biggest shareholders on the market at the end of 1996 were the OM Group with a 20.7 percent slice, S-E-Banken with 10.9 percent, Handelsbanken with 7.7 percent, Nordbanken and the National Debt Office with 6.8 percent each and Investor 6.7 percent.
Looking ahead, the exchange said income depends on share trading, making it hard to forecast.
Operating costs are expected to increase sharply, following increased investments and developing costs.
